correctness.rationale: The Green-function covariance gives Var(J)=1/180, cross-covariance G=(2c-1)(4c(1-c)-h²)/24 and observation variance D=c(1-c)-h/6+η>0. The posterior variance reduction is G²/D. Reflection and z=c(1-c) reduce all feasible locations to a compact interval. An exact derivative factorization with N''= -64 and explicit endpoint signs proves a unique interior optimum if S>0 or strict boundary optimality if S≤0, including all equality cases. Implicit derivatives prove inward movement with increasing noise; compact optimization yields the high-noise limit. Exact symbolic identities and independent quadrature checks passed; finite scans are supplementary.

value.rationale: Fixed-footprint boxcar measurements are natural finite-resolution sensors and linear inverse observations. The complete nontrivial phase diagram resolves whether a sensor should touch the spatial boundary, including an exact width constant, a positive noise-induced switch for intermediate widths, strict location response and an explicit high-noise limit. For h=1/4, η=1/5 the optimum improves variance explained by approximately 27.69% over boundary sensing. This is a meaningful constrained design fact independent of unavailable generalizations.
